clue.text: One hating Englishman's old pub in a new world

indicators.note: the old pub is placed in the middle of the new world phrase, splitting it open

parts.note: a globe is the world
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: A man who hates the English opens his traditional pub in a new country.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Englishman's reads as 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'in' splits the new world after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix Anglo- refers to the English and -phobe means a hater, so the word names someone with a dread of England.

clue.text: Pain in stomach eases

indicators.note: the letters sit within the run of the words stomach eases

explanation.surface: A sufferer reports that an abdominal pain is easing off.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull lasting pain is a simple synonym.

clue.text: Relative's piano, a piano that's upright

parts.note: a grand is a kind of piano

indicators.note: in a down clue, upright means the letters are written going upward, so read from the bottom

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A family member owns a piano, and specifically an upright one.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Relative reads as 'is'. A and P, set upright, give PA after GRAND; the surface's 'upright piano' is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is a family relative, and this is the familiar name for him.

clue.text: No longer at risk having sold certain golf clubs

definitions.meaning: idiom for being past danger or difficulty
woods are a type of golf club, so someone who has sold theirs is now without them, playfully read

explanation.surface: A golfer, now safe from trouble, has sold some clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means past danger, like someone emerging from a dangerous forest.

clue.text: Empty a shed in European country

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, so the letter a is dropped from the country

parts.note: Hungary is a country in central Europe

explanation.surface: A shed is left empty in some European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a noun in the surface, but it is the verb to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty stomach means one is in want of food, so empty here means famished.

clue.text: Ecstatic catching leader of fraud in fake US bills

indicators.note: the scrambled bills enclose, or catch, the other letter
fake bills are counterfeit, so the letters are rearranged
the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted at catching the head of a forgery ring with counterfeit dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake' rearranges US BILLS to BLISSUL, which takes in F from 'leader of fraud'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic and the answer are synonyms for extremely happy.

clue.text: Meat starter of mutton introduced by resort

indicators.note: the resort comes first and introduces the next letter

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dish of meat begins with mutton served up by a holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a brand of tinned luncheon meat, so meat is its general category.

clue.text: Composer docked pleasant vessel from South Island

indicators.note: in a down clue, read from the bottom up, the letters run backwards
a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant
a cup is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A composer arrives in a trimmed pleasure vessel from an island in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' turns NICE into NIC; 'from South' turns NIC+CUP into PUCCIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Puccini was the Italian who wrote the operas La Bohème and Tosca.

clue.text: I'm upset with guards making errors

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: sentries are guards on watch

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that the guards keep making mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IM into MI. 'making' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongly entered records or items are mistakes, a general synonym.

clue.text: Take courage try size down from twelve

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it
British clothing sizes go in steps of two, so the size below twelve is ten

explanation.surface: A shopper is told to be brave and try a smaller size.
explanation.walkthrough: UK women's dress sizes run 8, 10, 12, so one size down from twelve is ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cheered or emboldened is to take courage, an intransitive sense of the word.

clue.text: Dunce is entangling leads

indicators.note: entangled letters are knotted together into a new order

explanation.surface: A dunce gets tangled up in the dog leads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' looks like a noun for dog leashes, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone to act is to persuade or prompt them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Don't mention mounted trophy I've ordered paramour

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means raised up, so the letters run upwards

parts.note: an award is a trophy

indicators.note: the letters of the word are put in a new order

parts.note: a paramour is a lover

explanation.surface: Someone urges silence about the trophy a lover has had mounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns AWARD into DRAWA; 'ordered' turns I'VE into VEI.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to avoid talking about something embarrassing, as if it were covered up.

clue.text: Core of students warning: stop environmental change

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letters

parts.note: fore is the warning shout in golf
a station is a stop on a railway line

explanation.surface: Student activists sound a warning: halt environmental damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing forests is an environmental change, here an example of the broader phrase.

clue.text: Worry about American work, editor added detail

indicators.note: the worry wraps around the work

parts.note: to eat at someone is to worry them
labor is the American spelling of labour, meaning work

explanation.surface: Fussing over a piece of American writing, an editor added detail.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand on something is to fill it out with more particulars.

clue.text: Abhor husband being enthralled by gloater endlessly

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so the husband is held inside
endlessly means without its end letters

explanation.surface: A wife detests her husband for being captivated by a smug gloater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' turns GLOATER into LOATE, which takes in H.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhor and the answer both mean to detest intensely.

clue.text: Comparatively nauseated when one consumes rum? On the contrary

indicators.note: consumes means swallows, putting one piece inside another
the reverse of what is said: the rum is consumed, not consuming

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange, as is queer
as means when, in the sense of while
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone feels sicker when drinking rum, or rather the rum takes them over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'consumes': the rum does the swallowing, not the drinker. 'Rum' looks like the drink but is old British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling queasy means sick, and this is the comparative form.

clue.text: Prince redesigned court for district

indicators.note: something redesigned has its parts rearranged

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court, as in street names

explanation.surface: A prince has his court redesigned to serve a district.
explanation.definitionFit: A precinct is an area of a town or a police district, a synonym.

clue.text: Phone wife or daughter in new term

parts.note: to give someone a buzz is to phone them

explanation.surface: Someone calls a wife or daughter to share a fashionable new expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashionable word of the moment is a newly popular term.

clue.text: Flies, perhaps, ones that move fast

definitions.meaning: flies on trousers are an example of fastenings that zip up
things that whizz along at speed

explanation.definitionFit: Trouser flies are often zip fasteners, and something that moves at speed zips along.

clue.text: Item of furniture's firm support

parts.note: set means firm or hardened
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture has a solid supporting frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sofa for two is a piece of furniture, given here by category.

clue.text: Act deceitfully as sea god, keeping close to enemy

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: Triton is the Greek god of the sea, son of Poseidon

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A sea god plays tricks while holding an enemy close.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to attempt a deception and see whether one gets away with it.

clue.text: Shortened copper post

indicators.note: shortened means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: copper is slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: A copper has had their post cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like the metal but is a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is a job or position, the same sense as holding office.

clue.text: With disapproval, European interrupts cooking of phall curry

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so this letter sits inside the rest
cooking mixes the ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A European diner, appalled, interrupts the cooking of a fiery phall curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' mixes OF PHALL CURRY into RPROACHFULLY, and E goes inside. A phall is a fiercely hot curry from British curry houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a way that shows blame or disappointment means doing it with disapproval.

clue.text: Parisian's first person on wings of this aircraft

parts.note: je is French for I, the first person pronoun

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is the first passenger aboard this plane's wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places JE above TS in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Jets are jet-engined aircraft, a type within the broader class.

clue.text: Tense about a relative's betrayal

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
re means about, concerning
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a family member's treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after relative reads as 'is'. 'Tense' looks like the adjective for anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the betrayal of one's country, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Guest in capital of Vietnam is there regularly

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter
regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A visitor in the capital of Vietnam goes there often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Vietnam' looks like Hanoi but is just V.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been invited is a guest, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Table not totally made skilfully

indicators.note: only part of the letters of the words made skilfully are used

explanation.surface: A table only partly made with skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk is a kind of table used for writing or working.

clue.text: Soldiers circle armoured vehicles around German man

parts.note: O is the shape of a circle

indicators.note: the vehicles go around the man

parts.note: tanks are armoured fighting vehicles
Herr is the German word for Mr, a man

explanation.surface: Troops form a circle of tanks around a German.
explanation.definitionFit: The military phrase covers all soldiers who are not commissioned officers.
